messages:
maria: quick q — running into a weird CI-only 401 on windows-latest in GH Actions. local curl works. in the job I do `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/health` and the header ends up with literal quotes around the base64 value in the request. anyone seen GH Actions add quotes to secrets?
aj: hmmm — can you paste the workflow snippet for that step?
maria: sure, here's the step exactly as in our workflow:
```
name: CI
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: curl test
        env:
          API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
        run: |
          curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/health
```
kevin: Windows runners default to cmd/pwsh behavior depending on the step. `echo -n` isn't available in cmd and pwsh has different var access (`$env:API_KEY`). YAML interpolation + the runner shell can add or preserve quotes. also if the secret contains whitespace or special chars it sometimes gets quoted.
aj: two quick fixes: set `shell: bash` on that step so the `echo -n` and `$(...)` work as expected, or do the base64 entirely in powershell. example powershell snippet:
```powershell
# pwsh in GH Actions
$bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$env:API_KEY:")
[Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
```
aj: or if you prefer to stick with bash on windows, explicitly set `shell: bash` then:
```bash
printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64
```
maria: tried `shell: bash` and that fixed it — header in the request now has no extra quotes and the health call succeeds. thanks! :raised_hands:
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: step 'curl test' succeeded on windows-latest
maria: i'll add a short note to our devex docs about GH Actions on windows + basic auth/header creation (pwsh vs bash) so others don't hit this.
